source.version: arXiv:2412.18940v2, 14 February 2025 (CHI 2025 manuscript); full text including Appendices A-C
source.title_on_document: Amuse: Human-AI Collaborative Songwriting with Multimodal Inspirations

supplement.where: Appendices A-C, PDF pp. 24-28. The project page for sound examples and code is https://yewon-kim.com/amuse (PDF p. 1, footnote 1).
supplement.holds: System prompts, chord-model implementation details, additional keyword-relevance evaluation (Table 4), survey and interview questions, and thematic-analysis codebooks (Tables 5-6).

paper_design_summary: In supervised Zoom sessions, 10 songwriters each composed choruses using Amuse plus Aria and Aria alone, with both task prompts and system conditions randomized across sessions (PDF pp. 11-12, Sections 7.1-7.2). The study compared post-task self-reports, interviews, and interaction logs; creativity and composition quality were self-perceived, with no independent or computed creativity/diversity score on the songwriters' work (PDF p. 12, Section 7.3; pp. 17-18, Section 8.3; p. 26, Appendix C.1). Separate components comprised formative interviews with eight hobbyists, automated chord-generation benchmarks, and 45 analyzed listeners judging model-generated clips (PDF p. 3, Section 3.1; pp. 9-11, Section 6).

studies.label: User study: songwriting with Amuse plus Aria versus Aria alone (Sections 7-8; supervised remote sessions)

assignment.what_was_assigned: The order of the Assist (Amuse plus Aria) and Baseline (Aria alone) conditions and the songwriting prompts across each participant's sessions. Each songwriter experienced both conditions; this was a supervised Zoom experiment, coded lab_rct under the codebook's supervised-session definition.
assignment.quote: Both task prompts and system conditions were randomized across the sessions to minimize the ordering bias.
assignment.locator: PDF p. 12, Section 7.2 (Study Procedure); p. 11, Section 7.2 defines the conditions and remote Zoom setting.

arms.name: Assist
arms.description: Amuse and Aria available within Hookpad. The same 10 songwriters completed this condition (PDF p. 11, Sections 7.1-7.2 and Table 3; p. 14, Figure 8).

arms.name: Baseline
arms.description: Aria alone within Hookpad. The same 10 songwriters completed this condition; the two condition counts must not be added (PDF p. 11, Sections 7.1-7.2 and Table 3; p. 16, Figure 10).

participants.who: Active Hooktheory/Hookpad songwriters recruited through targeted email outreach: eight hobbyists and two professionals, all songwriting at least weekly. The analysis includes the same 10 people in both conditions. The paper does not separately report a count at randomization, so n_randomized is null.
participants.quote: We recruited 10 songwriters through targeted email outreach to active Hooktheory users, ensuring that our study included genuine songwriters actively engaging with the platform.
participants.locator: PDF p. 11, Section 7.1 and Table 3; p. 14, Figure 8 and Section 8.2.1; p. 16, Figure 10 and Section 8.2.2; p. 18, Figure 11.

ai_tool.name_model: Amuse (gpt-4o-2024-05-13 with LSTM-based rejection sampling) plus Aria, versus Aria alone
ai_tool.how_used: Amuse converts user-provided text/images into editable music keywords and generates chord progressions, and can transcribe chords from audio. Suggestions can be inserted and edited in Hookpad. Aria generates contextual chord/melody continuations or infills. Participants had to use their assigned tool(s) at least once but chose when and how to use them (PDF pp. 5-7, Sections 4.1-4.4; pp. 11-12, Section 7.2).

task.description: Compose an 8-bar chorus of chords and melodies for each of two prompts: an unexpected friendship and a favorite summer holiday memory. Post-task questionnaires assess perceived songwriting experience and Creativity Support Index items; interviews and interaction logs assess the process. No independent or computed creativity/diversity scoring of the participants' compositions is reported (PDF pp. 11-12, Sections 7.2-7.3; p. 26, Appendix C.1).
task.duration: 25 minutes allowed per songwriting session; two sessions within a 2-hour study (PDF pp. 11-12, Sections 7.1-7.2 and Figure 6).

outcomes.name: CSI Expressiveness: self-reported expressiveness and creativity during the activity
outcomes.question: none

contrasts.reported: Post-task self-report on a seven-point agreement scale, not a creativity score on the composition: Expressiveness, Assist=6.00±0.63, Baseline=4.20±1.66, z=4.00, p=0.028. The paper specifies a Wilcoxon signed-rank test and labels the statistic z.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 17, Section 8.3.2; p. 18, Figure 11; p. 12, Section 7.3.1 (test); p. 26, Appendix C.1 (scale and item).

outcomes.name: CSI Exploration: self-reported ease of exploring options, ideas, designs, or outcomes
outcomes.question: none

contrasts.reported: Post-task self-report on a seven-point agreement scale: Exploration, Assist=6.10±0.83, Baseline=4.40±1.50, z=3.00, p=0.019. This is perceived exploration, not a count or score of produced ideas. The paper specifies a Wilcoxon signed-rank test and labels the statistic z.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 17, Section 8.3.2; p. 18, Figure 11; p. 12, Section 7.3.1 (test); p. 26, Appendix C.1 (scale and item).

outcomes.name: Musical Coherence: self-perceived coherence of the participant's own composition
outcomes.question: none

contrasts.reported: Post-task self-report on a seven-point agreement scale: Musical Coherence, Assist=6.00±1.18, Baseline=6.00±0.89, z=10.50, p=1.00. This is the songwriter's own perceived quality, not an independent output evaluation. The paper specifies a Wilcoxon signed-rank test and labels the statistic z.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 18, Section 8.3.4 and Figure 11; p. 12, Section 7.3.1 (test); p. 26, Appendix C.1 (scale and item).

task.description: Choose which of two model-generated clips sounds more pleasant/natural and which better reflects supplied music keywords. Appendix B.3 adds CLAP keyword-relevance evaluation using the same synthetic audio. These assess model output, not creativity of participants' own productions (PDF pp. 10-11, Section 6.2.2 and Figure 5; pp. 25-26, Appendix B.3).

eligibility.reason: The main songwriting study explicitly randomized system conditions across each participant's sessions, satisfying the within-person random-order rule (PDF p. 12, Section 7.2). It analyzed only 10 people, each in both conditions, below the 50-person threshold (PDF p. 11, Section 7.1 and Table 3; pp. 14 and 16, Figures 8 and 10). Its creativity and composition-quality results are post-task self-reports rather than eligible creativity/diversity scores on participant-produced outputs (PDF p. 12, Section 7.3; pp. 17-18, Section 8.3; p. 26, Appendix C.1). The eight formative interviewees and 45 analyzed listeners belong to separate study components and cannot be added to the songwriter sample (PDF p. 3, Section 3.1; p. 10, Section 6.2.2 and footnote 2). Technical evaluations concern generated chord suggestions, including model-distribution matching to a music corpus, and do not supply an eligible human-assistance outcome (PDF pp. 9-11, Section 6). This small randomized study with self-reported creativity is omitted from the core and from the codebook's context classes.

one_line_finding: With randomized condition order, 10 songwriters reported greater expressiveness with Amuse plus Aria than Aria alone (6.00±0.63 versus 4.20±1.66, p=0.028), while self-rated musical coherence was identical in mean (6.00 in both conditions, p=1.00); these are self-reports, not independently scored creative outputs (PDF pp. 11-12, Sections 7.1-7.2; p. 17, Section 8.3.2; p. 18, Section 8.3.4).
